faq.a: Aryaan is associated with the Persian form آریان, whose core sense is aryan; iranian, noble.

faq.q: What is the origin of Aryaan?
faq.a: Aryaan is associated with Persian. Āryān, from the Persian ethnonym āryā ('Aryan, noble'). The source record's gloss 'Lion, Noble, King' is an approximation. The source record classified it as Arabic, which is incorrect.
No — the underlying form is Persian, not Arabic.
Aryaan can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Persian-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.

faq.a: Romanization variants include Aryaan, aryaan, aryan. Script forms are آریان, आर्यान.

faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
